formats.key: exactInputSingle((address tokenIn,address tokenOut,uint24 fee,address recipient,uint256 deadline,uint256 amountIn,uint256 amountOutMinimum,uint160 sqrtPriceLimitX96) params)
effects: Exactly amountIn of tokenIn is pulled from the signer to the pool; when tokenIn is WETH and the router holds enough ETH, the signer's sent ETH is wrapped and paid instead.
Native ETH sent as msg.value leaves the signer; any part not used for a WETH payment stays in the router.
At least amountOutMinimum of tokenOut goes to recipient, or the call reverts.
A nonzero sqrtPriceLimitX96 can stop the swap early and spend less than amountIn.
The call reverts after the deadline.
formats.shown: Swap <amountIn tokenIn> for at least <amountOutMinimum tokenOut>, with the recipient, deadline, pool fee and ETH sent; a nonzero price limit is shown raw.

findings.title: exactInputSingle labels WETH as 'Amount to Send' when native ETH is what actually leaves.
findings.evidence: Case 0: the screen shows 'Amount to Send 0.551044464601797306 WETH' and 'ETH Sent 0.551044464601797306 ETH'. The mined signer effect is native ETH out only; the router wraps it (PeripheryPayments.pay: token == WETH9 && address(this).balance >= value -> deposit). No WETH leaves the signer. The reader was unsure 'whether it spends WETH, native ETH, or both'.
findings.fix: Relabel the field 'Amount to Swap' (paid from ETH sent when tokenIn is WETH and ETH is attached).

findings.title: exactInputSingle shows a nonzero price limit as a raw sqrtPriceX96 number.
findings.evidence: descriptor field params.sqrtPriceLimitX96 has format raw with visible mustMatch [0]. SwapRouter.exactInputInternal passes it to pool.swap, where it can stop the swap partway.
findings.fix: No format turns sqrtPriceX96 into a price; keep it visible as it is.

cases.notes: ETH out is shown by 'ETH Sent'; DACITY in with a bound of 0 goes to the signer. The extra WETH line confused the reader but did not change what they expected.

formats.key: exactOutputSingle((address tokenIn,address tokenOut,uint24 fee,address recipient,uint256 deadline,uint256 amountOut,uint256 amountInMaximum,uint160 sqrtPriceLimitX96) params)
effects: The pool decides amountIn, capped at amountInMaximum; that much tokenIn is pulled from the signer, or paid from the signer's sent ETH when tokenIn is WETH.
Exactly amountOut of tokenOut goes to recipient when the price limit is 0.
All msg.value leaves the signer; ETH the swap does not use stays in the router and is not refunded in this call.
The call reverts after the deadline.
formats.shown: Swap at most <amountInMaximum tokenIn> for <amountOut tokenOut>, with the recipient, deadline, pool fee and ETH sent.

findings.title: exactOutputSingle 'at most' wording hides that unused ETH stays in the router.
findings.evidence: SwapRouter.exactOutputSingle never refunds msg.value; PeripheryPayments.pay wraps only 'value' and refundETH sends address(this).balance to whoever calls it. The descriptor says 'Swap at most {params.amountInMaximum} for {params.amountOut}' and shows ETH Sent with no note.
findings.fix: Add a note or label saying ETH sent above the amount actually used is not returned unless refundETH runs in the same multicall.

findings.title: exactOutputSingle shows a nonzero price limit as a raw sqrtPriceX96 number.
findings.evidence: field params.sqrtPriceLimitX96 format raw. With a nonzero limit, exactOutputInternal skips the require(amountOutReceived == amountOut) check, so less than amountOut can arrive.
findings.fix: None possible beyond keeping it visible.

cases.notes: 39.538 ADI out, within the 40.339 maximum; exactly 321.2412 USDC in to the signer.

effects: The router's whole ETH balance, including any msg.value, is sent to the signer.
Native ETH sent with the call leaves the signer and comes straight back.
formats.shown: Refund ETH held by the router, with ETH sent.

formats.key: selfPermit(address token,uint256 value,uint256 deadline,uint8 v,bytes32 r,bytes32 s)
effects: Calls token.permit(signer, router, value, ...), which sets the signer's allowance for the router to value and uses up a permit nonce.
Any ETH sent stays in the router.
formats.shown: Let router spend <value token>, with ETH sent; unlimited above the threshold.

formats.key: selfPermitAllowed(address token,uint256 nonce,uint256 expiry,uint8 v,bytes32 r,bytes32 s)
effects: Calls a DAI-style permit with allowed=true, which sets the signer's allowance for the router to the maximum.
Any ETH sent stays in the router.
formats.shown: Let router spend all <token>, with ETH sent.

formats.key: selfPermitAllowedIfNecessary(address token,uint256 nonce,uint256 expiry,uint8 v,bytes32 r,bytes32 s)
effects: When the current allowance is below the maximum, calls a DAI-style permit, which sets the router's allowance to the maximum.
Any ETH sent stays in the router.
formats.shown: Let router spend all <token>, with ETH sent.

formats.key: selfPermitIfNecessary(address token,uint256 value,uint256 deadline,uint8 v,bytes32 r,bytes32 s)
effects: When the signer's allowance for the router is below value, calls token.permit, which sets the allowance to value.
Any ETH sent stays in the router.
formats.shown: Let router spend <value token>, with ETH sent.

findings.title: selfPermitIfNecessary on WETH claims an approval, but WETH's fallback silently does nothing.
findings.evidence: Case 6: the screen says 'Let router spend 0.012 WETH'. The mined effects show only a 0-amount WETH deposit from the router, i.e. the permit call hit WETH9's fallback (SelfPermit.selfPermit -> IERC20Permit(token).permit). No approval was granted.
findings.fix: No descriptor change can detect a token without permit; wallets could warn when the token is WETH9.

cases.notes: No signer effect; the reader believed a 0.012 WETH allowance was set, which did not happen.

effects: The router's entire balance of token, which must be at least amountMinimum, is sent to recipient.
Any ETH sent stays in the router.
formats.shown: Sweep at least <amountMinimum token> to <recipient>, with the token, recipient and ETH sent.

cases.notes: 0.016286 WETH arrived at the signer, equal to the minimum.

formats.key: sweepTokenWithFee(address token,uint256 amountMinimum,address recipient,uint256 feeBips,address feeRecipient)
effects: The router's whole token balance (at least amountMinimum, checked before the fee) is split: feeBips/10000 to feeRecipient, the rest to recipient.
feeBips must be between 1 and 100.
Any ETH sent stays in the router.
formats.shown: Sweep at least <amountMinimum token> less <feeBips>% fee to <recipient>, with the fee, fee recipient and ETH sent.

effects: The router's whole WETH balance (at least amountMinimum) is unwrapped and sent as ETH to recipient; none of the signer's WETH is touched.
Any ETH sent stays in the router.
formats.shown: Unwrap at least <amountMinimum ETH> to <recipient>, with ETH sent.

findings.title: unwrapWETH9 intent does not say it unwraps router-held WETH, not the signer's.
findings.evidence: PeripheryPayments.unwrapWETH9 uses IWETH9(WETH9).balanceOf(address(this)). The descriptor says 'Unwrap WETH' / 'Unwrap at least {amountMinimum} to {recipient}'. The case 9 reader believed 'WETH ... to Uniswap to be unwrapped' would leave their wallet; mined effects are empty.
findings.fix: interpolatedIntent: 'Unwrap WETH held by the router (at least {amountMinimum}) and send ETH to {recipient}'.

cases.notes: The router held no WETH; nothing moved. The reader wrongly expected WETH to leave their wallet.

effects: The router's whole WETH balance (at least amountMinimum, checked before the fee) is unwrapped; feeBips/10000 of it goes as ETH to feeRecipient and the rest to recipient.
feeBips must be between 1 and 100.
Any ETH sent stays in the router.
formats.shown: Unwrap at least <amountMinimum ETH> less <feeBips>% fee to <recipient>, with the fee, fee recipient and ETH sent.

findings.title: unwrapWETH9WithFee intent does not say the WETH is the router's balance.
findings.evidence: PeripheryPaymentsWithFee.unwrapWETH9WithFee reads IWETH9(WETH9).balanceOf(address(this)). The descriptor says 'Unwrap WETH' / 'Unwrap at least {amountMinimum} less {feeBips} fee to {recipient}'.
findings.fix: Say 'Unwrap WETH held by the router' in the interpolatedIntent.
